answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence depends on reachable attestations rather than self-assertion. A sybil cluster labeled ocean, lotus, or knoll can add many internal links, but a sparse external cut gives it low conductance. Under a fixed walk horizon and bounded per-node voting weight, conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds limit the probability mass entering the cluster, and therefore its aggregate voting weight.
